# v3.33.0

Covers everything since **v3.32.0**.

This release is mostly about **one training being one training**. A course typically arrives from imports under several slightly different names, all mapping to the same Full Title. Everything that *counts* already treated those as one training — but the catalogue still made you edit each spelling separately, and a few things quietly counted them as separate trainings. That is now consistent, and closing the gap uncovered two real defects along the way.

It also **stops two pages reporting on a company you did not choose**, corrects **two figures in Compliance Planning**, and opens up more of the Programs work to the read-only API.

**There is no database migration in this release.** Some reported figures will change, because they were wrong before — see *For administrators* at the end.

## Fixed — two pages reported on a company you never picked

With the company switcher set to **All companies**, the **program compliance dashboard** and **Compliance Planning** did not stop and ask. They quietly picked whichever company sorted first and drew a complete, confident report for it — with nothing on the page saying which company you were looking at.

Both now ask you to choose a company first, and show nothing until you do. The program dashboard also loses its own separate Company dropdown, which was a second control that could disagree with the one in the header.

This is worth reading twice if you have several companies: the figures you saw on those two pages under "All companies" were real figures, for one tenant, chosen alphabetically.

## Changed — edit a training once, not once per imported name

The Training Data catalogue now presents **one card per training** — that is, per Full Title and type — instead of one row per imported spelling.

Product, Function, Link, "Leads to certification" and OLX membership are set **once** and applied to every spelling. Previously an online course that had arrived under four names needed the same certification ticked four times, and it was easy to set three and miss one. Where the existing spellings currently disagree on a field, the page says so before you save, since saving will level them.

What stays per-spelling is what genuinely belongs to one: renaming it, moving it to another Full Title, deleting it, and its **type** — because the type is what decides which training a name belongs to, and changing it is the most destructive edit available.

Two smaller things from using the page for real:

- **The relationship pickers now show what you have selected.** They are scroll boxes over a catalogue that can run to hundreds of entries, so a tick five screens down was invisible. Selected entries are now pinned to the top, and they stay visible while you type in the search box — narrowing a search previously looked as though your selection had been cleared.
- **The quick, everyday fields come first** on the page, with the actions that take a training out of circulation last.

## Fixed — a rename could destroy program and offering requirements

Two defects underneath the change above, both reproduced against a real database before being changed.

- **Renaming a training silently deleted every program and offering requirement that named it.** There was no warning and no error; the requirements were simply gone afterwards, and nothing recorded that they had ever existed.
- **Renaming a training that anyone had actually completed failed outright**, with an unexplained error.

Both are fixed, and fixed in a way that covers requirement types added in future rather than just the ones that exist today. Renaming a training onto a name that already exists is now **refused** rather than silently merging the two groups — merging is available as its own explicit action, because the old behaviour could not be undone or even traced afterwards.

Separately, **deleting or renaming a training used to leave other trainings pointing at a name that no longer existed.** That failed silently too: the screen showed a raw internal key where a name should be, and the reports quietly stopped matching people. Those references are now updated or cleared properly.

## Fixed — reports counted a training by each spelling

Four reporting paths counted "leads to certification" and legacy-replacement relationships by the exact imported name rather than by the training.

The visible effect: **someone who held a different spelling of the certification was reported as not having it.** They appeared in Trained But Not Certified, and in the Legacy Replacement Gap report, when they had in fact completed the training. Any spelling whose relationships had been left blank was skipped entirely, so its learners never appeared at all.

The same applies to **online course completion**. An online course is complete when its sub-items are, and sub-items were being matched by exact name — so a course listing two spellings of one sub-item could only be completed by someone who had taken that course twice, under both names. In practice, nobody.

## New — Catalogue Integrity scan

Online course completions are recorded when something happens — an import, or an edit to the learner or the course — and nothing reconciles them afterwards. So the correction above does not reach people retrospectively: a learner who **already** satisfies the corrected rule will not receive their completion until something touches their record again.

Data Clean-Up therefore has a new, read-only **Catalogue Integrity** section that finds them, together with two fixes you can apply from it:

- **Missing online course completions** — learners who meet the rule but have no completion recorded, and any holding a completion the rule no longer supports (both directions are shown, so the scan is its own preview).
- **Uneven "leads to certification"** — where the spellings of one training disagree about which certifications they lead to. Levelling them takes the union, so no spelling can lose a certification it already had.

The scan shows what each fix will do before you run it. **Run it after updating** — see *For administrators*.

## Fixed — two figures in Compliance Planning

- **A wider renewal window could report fewer at-risk renewals than a narrower one.** A 3-month window showed more than a 6- or 12-month one, which is plainly backwards. The at-risk panel was limited to the specialisations on the recommended path — and which specialisations those are itself depends on the window, so widening it could shift the path and make expiring people disappear from the panel. Every at-risk renewal is now listed, marked according to whether the plan is costed against it, and the table and PDF separate the two.

- **A tier target badged more specialisations "Recommended" than it asked you to achieve.** Where achieving three more specialisations was recommended, four could be flagged. Exactly as many are now recommended as the headline asks for, and a genuine equal-cost swap is shown separately as an alternative rather than as a second recommendation.

Tier recommendations are also now chosen better. A certification required by two specialisations was being charged twice when ranking them, so the pair that looked cheapest routinely was not; each specialisation is now ranked by what it actually adds on top of the others.

## New — more of Programs available over the API

The read-only API gains four endpoints:

- **Compliance planning** — the roadmap, each requirement's gap and cost, the requirements that expiries put at risk, and the totals.
- **Program compliance trend** — twelve months of history plus a twelve-month forecast, per program and specialisation.
- **Renewal forecast** — projected renewals against lapses over the next twelve months.
- **An OpenAPI description** of the whole API, so an integration can generate a client rather than transcribing endpoints by hand. A copy is also published in the project's `docs` folder for reading before you hold a key.

**Compliance planning is returned as aggregates only.** The planner in the application also shows *who* to certify — named candidates, the full eligible pool, and the people whose training lapses inside the renewal window. **None of those reach the API.** A key receives the shape and the cost of a gap without receiving a roster of named staff. Nothing analytical is lost: the at-risk summary describes the same set the named list enumerates, and the totals carry its count.

Alongside that, the heavier API endpoints are now cached for up to 30 seconds, matching the application's own pages. Any change made in the application clears that immediately, so an integration never sees data from before an import or an edit.

## For administrators

**No database migration, and nothing to run by hand.**

**Some figures will change after updating, because they were wrong before.** Specifically, Trained But Not Certified and the Legacy Replacement Gap report will generally show **fewer** gaps — people who held a differently-spelled version of a certification were being reported as lacking it. Online course completion counts may go **up** for the same reason. If you compare against figures recorded before this release, expect them to differ.

**Run the Catalogue Integrity scan once after updating** (Data Clean-Up → Catalogue Integrity). It reports learners who now qualify for an online course completion but have not been given one, because those are only recorded when something touches the record. The scan is read-only; the fixes are applied only when you ask for them, and it shows you what each will do first.

**If you have more than one company**, be aware that the program dashboard and Compliance Planning now require you to select one, where they previously showed a report for whichever company sorted first.
